_comment: Toolchain pin for the layout/ verification flow (klt drc / klt extract /
klt lvs), checked (not merely recorded) before either runner does
anything -- the layout/ analogue of sim/toolchain.json's ngspice/PDK pin.
Why this is a CAPABILITY list, not a version number: `klt --version`
reports klayout-tools' own static pyproject.toml version, which moves
only when upstream cuts one -- it did not change across the ~150
commits between issue #15's pin and #51's ('0.1.0' at both), and this
pin's own bump moved it only from '0.1.0' to '0.2.0' while adding four
capabilities this repo depends on. A version string comparison would
therefore silently pass against a `klt` that is missing something this
repo needs. `klt_required_commands` is the coarse drift-detectable pin:
both runners look every entry up in `klt --help`'s subcommand list
before doing anything else and fail loudly, with the install command in
the error text, if one is missing -- exercised directly by running the
#51 bring-up against the release issue #15 pinned (no `extract`/`lvs`)
before upgrading. One shared implementation, in
`layout/toolchain_pin.py`, imported by both `layout/drc/run_drc.py` and
`layout/lvs/run_lvs.py` -- a per-runner copy would let the two drift
apart, and this claim is only worth making if it is true of both.
A verb list is NOT sufficient on its own any more, and that gap is
closed where it can be seen rather than argued: this repo now depends
on the gf180mcu extraction DECK recognising a device class
(`cap_mim_2f0_m4m5_noshield`), which every `klt` since `lvs` landed has
the verbs for. `layout/lvs/cells/cells.json`'s `extract.expect.
device_classes` pins the deck's own declared class list and
`run_lvs.py` asserts it, so an install from before that recognition
landed fails with a named mismatch instead of silently extracting the
CDAC unit capacitor as ordinary interconnect (issue #70).
Why `klt_install` names an exact commit and not a floating `git+URL`:
verified directly while implementing #51 that `main` is not safe to
float against here -- an upstream deck gaining coverage is a change
this repo's committed negative controls and manifests have to absorb
deliberately, in one reviewed change, not silently on the next
reinstall.
THIS PIN (issue #70) is that deliberate absorption, and it crosses two
upstream changes the previous pin (`e08f24f`) deliberately sat before:
* `1d5fc60` (PR #192) added gf180mcu DRC coverage for the MiM
capacitor stack and Metal2-5/MetalTop. It is what makes
`layout/drc/cells/uncovered_layer_probe.gds` -- issue #15's negative
control, drawn to prove the deck was NOT looking at those layers --
report real violations. `cells.json`'s expectations for that cell
are re-baselined in the same change, from `clean` to the four rules
it now catches. That is `layout/README.md`'s own 'useful failure:
it tells us the gap closed', taken.
* `0aa8bc2`/`fd22b7d` (PRs #238/#235) populated the extraction deck's
full Metal1-Metal5 / Via1-Via4 stack and added MiM capacitor device
recognition. Together they are what let a drawn unit capacitor be a
CHECKED device instead of three inert polygons.
and picks up `c6fa8b8`/`de4b8dc` (`klt extract --parasitics`) on the
way, which is what issue #17 needs and could not have without this bump.
klt_install            exact commit to install `klt` from -- a `pip`/
`uv tool install` VCS URL pinned with `@<sha>`
(no PyPI release yet, ../README.md), not a
floating branch reference. See above for why
floating is unsafe for this repo specifically.
klt_required_commands  every `klt <command>` this repo's layout/
runners invoke. A missing one is a tooling
error (exit 1) from *either* runner, not a
silently-skipped check. Adding an entry here is
all it takes to make both runners require it.
klt_last_verified_commit  the exact commit `klt_install` resolves to,
restated here so it is visible without
parsing the install URL. Update both together
and re-run both runners' --check when bumping.
klayout_package_min    floor for the pip `klayout` package version
(`klayout_tools`' own `pyproject.toml` pins
`klayout>=0.29`); recorded here so a drift in
*this* repo's pin is visible next to `klt`'s.
A drift in `klt_required_commands` is fatal by default; there is no
--allow-toolchain-drift override here (unlike sim/toolchain.json) --
layout/ evidence is cheap enough to regenerate that skipping the check
has no use case yet.
